hero.title: US–Iran Conflict Escalates as Oil Markets Face Fresh Supply Risks
hero.description: The US–Iran confrontation intensified after US forces struck three Iranian oil carriers following Iranian ballistic-missile attacks on two US Navy ships. Meanwhile, a devastating disaster in Nepal, an eruption in Indonesia and a major German state election dominate the international agenda.

featured.title: US–Iran Conflict Sends New Shock Through Global Energy Markets
featured.content: The confrontation between the United States and Iran has intensified again. US Central Command said American forces struck three Iranian crude-oil carriers on Saturday after Iran's Revolutionary Guard launched ballistic missiles towards two US Navy ships. No American personnel were reported injured. Iranian forces also fired at vessels near Iran and warned ships over movements through the Strait of Hormuz. Brent crude moved as high as about $96.28 a barrel amid renewed fears of disruption to global energy supplies.

articles.title: US–Iran confrontation escalates around oil shipping routes
articles.content: The United States and Iran exchanged fire around vessels near Iranian waters on Saturday. US Central Command said it struck three Iranian crude carriers after Iranian ballistic missiles were launched at two US Navy ships. The confrontation is increasing concerns about energy supplies and commercial shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.
articles.imageQuery: US Iran oil tanker Strait of Hormuz

articles.title: Oil prices remain under pressure as Middle East risks increase
articles.content: Renewed military exchanges between Washington and Tehran are keeping crude markets highly volatile. Brent crude reached about $96.28 a barrel on Saturday as traders assessed the possibility of further disruption to oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz.

articles.title: US envoys hold lengthy talks with Putin over Ukraine war
articles.content: US representatives Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner held more than three hours of talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow. Russian officials described the discussions as useful, but no breakthrough was announced. The US delegation is expected to continue diplomatic engagement with Ukraine.

articles.title: Nigeria's Dangote Refinery IPO receives SEC approval
articles.content: Nigeria's Securities and Exchange Commission has approved the planned IPO of Dangote Refinery. The offering involves 4.1 billion shares priced at ₦525 each and could raise approximately ₦2.15 trillion if fully subscribed. The order book is expected to open on September 14. Dangote plans to use the capital to support expansion towards 1.4 million barrels per day.

articles.title: Nigeria kidnapping crisis continues to worry families
articles.content: Families of people abducted in Nigeria continue to demand information and action as the country's security crisis persists. The prolonged uncertainty surrounding missing victims is renewing calls for stronger intelligence gathering, coordinated security operations and better protection for vulnerable communities.

articles.title: Africa backs move towards a more accurate world map
articles.content: The United Nations has backed a resolution supporting wider use of a map that more accurately represents the relative size of Africa and other regions, challenging the distortions associated with the centuries-old Mercator projection.
articles.imageQuery: Africa map United Nations world map

articles.title: Germany votes in closely watched Saxony-Anhalt election
articles.content: Voters in Saxony-Anhalt are going to the polls in an election that could become a landmark moment for Germany's far-right AfD. The party has been polling above 40%, ahead of Chancellor Friedrich Merz's CDU. A major breakthrough could strengthen the AfD's ambitions ahead of the 2029 federal election.

articles.title: Berlin investigates major ransomware data leak
articles.content: Berlin's state government says it is conducting an intensive review after a large quantity of stolen data was published following a ransomware attack. Authorities are assessing the scope of the breach and its potential consequences.

articles.title: Nepal disaster leaves more than 1,300 dead and thousands missing
articles.content: Nepal is continuing a huge search and rescue operation after catastrophic floods and an ice-rock avalanche devastated communities on August 26. More than 1,300 people have died and more than 5,600 remain missing across the affected region. Rescue teams are still searching tunnels and other areas where workers may remain trapped.

articles.title: Chinese worker rescued alive after 10 days inside Nepal tunnel
articles.content: A Chinese national was rescued alive from a 225-metre hydropower tunnel in Nepal after spending 10 days underground. The rescue followed the recovery of two other survivors from another flooded tunnel the previous day, offering fresh hope to families still waiting for news.

articles.title: Anak Krakatau eruption disrupts hundreds of flights
articles.content: Indonesia's Anak Krakatau volcano has erupted, sending ash plumes up to around 50,000 feet over parts of Java and Sumatra. Authorities suspended 209 flights at Jakarta's Soekarno-Hatta International Airport and cancelled some school activities and fishing trips. Officials said there was no immediate tsunami threat.

articles.title: South Korea's exports surpass last year's full-year record
articles.content: South Korea's exports have reached $709.4 billion so far this year, already exceeding the country's previous full-year record. Strong demand for advanced technology products, particularly AI-related semiconductors, has helped drive the increase.
articles.imageQuery: South Korea semiconductor exports AI chips

articles.title: Global energy markets remain highly sensitive to Middle East conflict
articles.content: Crude prices are heading for a sharp weekly gain as renewed US–Iran hostilities raise concerns over oil supplies. The Strait of Hormuz remains a major focus because disruption there could affect global energy flows and increase inflationary pressure.
articles.imageQuery: global oil market crude oil trading

articles.title: Cybersecurity concerns grow after Berlin data leak
articles.content: Authorities in Berlin are investigating a large stolen-data publication linked to a ransomware attack. The incident highlights continuing risks for governments and public institutions as cybercriminal groups target sensitive systems.

articles.title: US Supreme Court revives discounted political advertising policy
articles.content: The US Supreme Court on Friday revived a federal policy allowing political party committees to access discounted television and radio advertising rates previously available to candidates. The decision comes ahead of the November midterm elections.

articles.title: RadiantWaves verification warning: viral conflict videos require caution
articles.content: As the US–Iran conflict develops, social media users are being exposed to old footage, misleading clips and AI-generated material presented as current events. RadiantWaves Media recommends checking the source, date and independent confirmation before treating viral footage as evidence.

morningSummary: Good morning. Sunday begins with renewed concern over the US–Iran conflict, rising energy-market risks, a devastating disaster in Nepal and a major volcanic eruption in Indonesia. Nigeria also has a major business development with SEC approval of the Dangote Refinery IPO. In Europe, Germany's Saxony-Anhalt election could have major political implications, while the US Open continues in New York.
bigQuestion: With wars threatening energy supplies and natural disasters causing enormous destruction, should governments invest more in prevention and preparedness rather than waiting to respond after disaster strikes?
quoteOfTheDay: A peaceful future is built by people who choose wisdom over fear, preparation over panic, and truth over rumours.
